title: Passholder, Multi-Booking and Sibling Reduction Rates Across the Snowsports School Range
content:
Three reduction rates are published against each Snowsports School product: whether a season passholder reduction is taken off the product at all, the percentage taken off where the household books the product for several participants at once, and the percentage taken off the second and each further child of one household booked into the product.

| Product | Passholder reduction carried | Multi-booking reduction | Sibling reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| All-Mountain Adult Group Lesson | yes | 5.00 percent | 0.00 percent |
| Mountain Explorers Group Lesson | yes | 5.00 percent | 10.00 percent |
| Mountain Cubs Group Lesson | yes | 5.00 percent | 10.00 percent |
| Six-Week Development Programme | yes | 10.00 percent | 15.00 percent |
| Semi-Private Coaching Session | yes | 7.50 percent | 0.00 percent |
| Private Instruction Full Day | yes | 10.00 percent | 0.00 percent |
| Elite Performance Camp | no | 0.00 percent | 0.00 percent |

## Comparing the rates

- Six of the seven products carry a season passholder reduction. The Elite Performance Camp carries none, and its multi-booking and sibling reductions both stand at 0.00 percent.
- The multi-booking reduction runs from 5.00 percent on the three products at that figure, through 7.50 percent on the Semi-Private Coaching Session, to 10.00 percent on the Six-Week Development Programme and the Private Instruction Full Day.
- A sibling reduction stands above nothing on three products only: 10.00 percent on the Mountain Explorers Group Lesson and the Mountain Cubs Group Lesson, and 15.00 percent on the Six-Week Development Programme, the highest rate in the range.
- On the Six-Week Development Programme the sibling reduction of 15.00 percent stands above that product's multi-booking reduction of 10.00 percent; on the Mountain Explorers Group Lesson and the Mountain Cubs Group Lesson the sibling reduction of 10.00 percent stands above the multi-booking reduction of 5.00 percent.
